clauses.reason: Section 1-101 authorizes the Attorney General, under section 102(a)(1) of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1802(a)), to approve electronic surveillance to acquire foreign intelligence information without a court order, but only on the certifications the Act requires. It has no end of its own, no held later instrument touches it, and the held text of 50 U.S.C. 1802(a)(1) still provides that the President, through the Attorney General, may authorize such surveillance on those certifications.

clauses.reason: Section 1-103 designates the listed officials to make the certifications required by the Act in support of surveillance applications, and says none of them nor anyone officially acting may certify unless appointed by the President with Senate consent. It continues as amended. Executive Order 13383 section 1 (2005-07-15) struck (c) Director of Central Intelligence and inserted (c) Director of National Intelligence, struck (g) Deputy Director of Central Intelligence and inserted (g) Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, and added (h) Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence. Executive Order 13475 section 1 (2008-10-07) struck the paragraph number (7) wherever it appears and inserted (6), added (i) Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and added a sentence that the Senate-appointment requirement does not apply to the Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended; the amendments change the list and a cross-reference, not the substance of the designation. Nothing held ends the clause.

Section 1-104 amended section 2-202 of Executive Order 12036 by inserting a sentence that electronic surveillance as defined in the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 shall be conducted in accordance with that Act as well as the order. Executive Order 12036 was revoked, with its amendments, by Executive Order 12333 section 3.6, signed 1981-12-04 (Executive Order No. 12036 of January 24, 1978, as amended, entitled United States Intelligence Activities, is revoked). The inserted sentence therefore ended with its parent text on that date, and no held source shows it was re-enacted. The current U.S. Code note brackets this section as an amendment of the revoked Executive Order 12036. The revocation date is the signing date on the held Federal Register text; no separate effective date is stated.

Section 1-105 amended section 2-203 of Executive Order 12036 by inserting a sentence that monitoring that constitutes electronic surveillance as defined in the Act shall be conducted in accordance with that Act as well as the order. Executive Order 12036 was revoked, with its amendments, by Executive Order 12333 section 3.6, signed 1981-12-04 (Executive Order No. 12036 of January 24, 1978, as amended, entitled United States Intelligence Activities, is revoked). The inserted sentence therefore ended with its parent text on that date, and no held source shows it was re-enacted. The current U.S. Code note brackets this section as an amendment of the revoked Executive Order 12036. The revocation date is the signing date on the held Federal Register text; no separate effective date is stated.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (44 FR 30311, signed 1979-05-23). The dossier inventory split section 1-103 into (a) to (g) fragments and left 1-101, 1-102, 1-104 and 1-105 unseparated, so the clause inventory is corrected to the five operative sections 1-101 to 1-105 by inventory override (absolute spans in the held Federal Register text). Sections 1-101 to 1-103 implement the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1802 and 1804): the Attorney General is authorized to approve warrantless surveillance on the statutory certifications, to approve applications to the court, and the listed officials are designated to make the certifications. Held later events: Executive Order 13383 (2005-07-15) and Executive Order 13475 (2008-10-07) amended section 1-103 and are attached from their official Federal Register texts. Sections 1-104 and 1-105 amended Executive Order 12036, which Executive Order 12333 revoked on 1981-12-04, ending those two amending commands. The held text of 50 U.S.C. 1802 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) still carries the delegation in its Executive Documents note as amended by Executive Orders 13383 and 13475, with sections 1-104 and 1-105 bracketed as having amended the revoked Executive Order 12036. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. Authority statute: 50 U.S.C. 1802 is held and in force; 50 U.S.C. 1804 is cited by the order and its text is not held.
